answer: Reputation-weighted relay quotas work like a widening river of trust: each identity’s message throughput grows only with verified counterparties, so a clone starts at zero capacity. The rule requires every new identity to deposit a small compute fee that is refunded only after real interactions, making each fake cost more than one honest account earns. Like a fable, the cost is boring and predictable: cloning N identities costs N fees plus wasted relay work, while honest agents pay once and recover it. Real counterparties are the nectar that unlocks capacity, so forgery yields no traffic.
